19.0.s.en: (1) The time and place of receiving the commandments

19.0.0.en: The time for receiving the commandments from God was in the third month after the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt. They had to pass through the barren wilderness, almost dying of thirst and hunger, and then God satisfied them with manna and water, which signify Christ, and in the third month, which signifies the Resurrection, they receive the commandment, just as Christ passed through death and rose on the third day.

19.1.0.en: It specifies that the place of receiving the commandments was in the wilderness of Sinai, in a wide valley with a great mountain before them, which it calls Mount Sinai, one of the known mountains in the wilderness of Sinai. They had moved from Rephidim, which is in the middle of the wilderness of Sinai toward the south, to the wilderness of Sinai, by which is meant the Sinai peninsula, that is, they moved a little toward the southeast (maps 1, 2). When man is stripped of the comfort of Egypt, that is, the comfort of the body and the pleasures of sin, he can in the barren wilderness hear the voice of God and enjoy His commandments.

19.1.1.en: Control your desires and do not give your body everything it asks, and your spirit will be refreshed and long for reading and prayer.

19.2.0.en: Moses was accustomed to speaking with God, so God called him from the mountain to come up to Him, and he went up to speak with Him. The people would not hear this voice, for it was for Moses alone, since he had a high spiritual rank in which he deserved to hear the voice of God.

19.2.1.en: In proportion to your longing for God, He lets you hear His voice, draws you near to Him, leads your life and gives you the joy of fellowship with Him. So take care to pray, that you may know God and hear Him.

19.3.0.en: God reminded Moses how He had rescued them from the mighty Egyptians and brought them out of the bondage of Egypt with a strong arm into the wilderness, and because of their faith in Him He lifted them up to Himself, to heaven, as an eagle seizes its prey and rises with it on high.

19.3.1.en: The eagles signify the Holy Spirit, who lifts us up to the heavenly things by faith and saves us from all dangers. Here appears the tenderness of God, who speaks with fatherhood, carrying His children like a little child, drawing them near to Him and rescuing them from the hands of the wicked.

19.4.0.en: God declared to Moses that if the people kept His commandments, which He would declare to them by Moses, He would grant them a special boldness, in that they would be a people distinguished for Him by His care, more than the rest of the peoples of the earth, which are all subject to God because He is the Creator of all.

19.4.1.en: Your care to carry out God's commandments gives you the joy of sonship to Him and of His care, for God is rich and gives to all who take refuge in Him, and distinguishes those who cling to Him.

19.5.0.en: In addition to His special care for them, God promises His people to give them the priesthood by which they draw near to Him through the sacrifices and all the rites, and He also promises them that they will be holy to Him, that is, set apart by His dwelling among them.

19.5.1.en: What is meant by "a kingdom of priests" is that there are priests in it, and here the special priesthood begins for the first time in the person of Aaron and his sons, for the head of the family used to be its priest before.

19.5.2.en: All these words God commanded Moses to declare to the people, so that, rejoicing in these promises, they might prepare to receive the commandments.

19.6.0.en: Moses gathered the elders of the children of Israel and declared to them everything God had said to him, so that they might know the word of God and teach it to the rest of the people.

19.7.0.en: The elders informed the people of God's words to Moses, and they rejoiced in His promises and declared their submission to God, and they came and told Moses so, although sadly they later turned back and left God when they worshipped the golden calf and when they murmured.

19.7.1.en: Do not be content with general promises to God, or with reading and hearing His voice in spiritual sermons, but would that you would strive to apply the word in your life.

19.8.0.en: When the people declared their submission and readiness to obey God's commandments, the Lord rejoiced in them and promised Moses to appear to all the people in a thick cloud, in dense fog. This declares the greatness of God and the inability of any human being to comprehend all that is in Him.

19.9.0.en: God asked Moses to prepare the people to see Him, by bodily purification, that is, the washing of their bodies today and the day after, as a symbol of inner purity, and the washing of clothes for the same purpose, and also by abstaining from bodily relations between husband and wife; their sanctification, that is, setting themselves apart for God and His worship, as they prepare to meet God. This also happens in the New Testament when husband and wife abstain from bodily relations before Communion.

19.10.0.en: Here is a confirmation of the idea of the Resurrection through the third day, in which God appears and gives His commandments while they have been purified for three days.

19.11.0.en: "Bounds": by setting marks such as pillars of stones or pits or any marks that the people may not pass around the holy mountain.

19.11.1.en: When God comes down upon the mountain, all of it becomes holy, like the altar in the temple of the New Testament, upon which God descends with His Body and Blood. Therefore He asked Moses to warn the people not to approach the mountain, and any man or beast that touches the mountain is put to death. This shows the holiness of God and that there must be no laxity in approaching Him, by repentance and confession before Communion. It also signifies spiritually the necessity of man's ridding himself of the sins of emotional attachment that hinder him from God, signified by the man who is put to death, and likewise the animal lusts, signified by the killing of the animal.

19.11.2.en: And when they hear the sound of the trumpet, which is either a sound coming from God or Moses commands one of his helpers to blow the trumpet, then those whom God chose, who are mentioned in (ch. 24), come forward to approach the mountain, and they are Moses, Aaron and his sons, and the seventy elders.

19.12.0.en: Moses instructed the people how to prepare, by washing their clothes and abstaining from marital relations, and the people obeyed. This is a clear teaching of the importance of chastity in married life when drawing near to God by partaking of the Holy Sacraments.

19.13.s.en: (4) The appearance of God on the mountain

19.13.0.en: At the time God had appointed, that is, after the people had been purified for three days, God appeared with the following:

19.13.1.en: 1- Thunders: loud sounds that declare the power of God.

19.13.2.en: 2- Lightnings: shining with brilliance, declaring the glory and splendor of God.

19.13.3.en: 3- A cloud: it signifies the presence of God, as happened at the Transfiguration, for it is white, dense and high in the heavens, so it declares the glory of God and also His depths, which no one knows.

19.13.4.en: 4- A trumpet: a loud sound to warn people for striving and war, meaning the feeling of the fear of God and readiness for Him.

19.13.5.en: And before the greatness of God the people were very afraid and trembled at His majesty.

19.13.6.en: The fear of God makes you keep away from every sin and enjoy fellowship with Him, and you no longer fear anything earthly.

19.14.0.en: Moses brought the people out of their tents inside the camp and stood them before the mountain, and they were in great fear because of the appearance of God.

19.15.0.en: The fifth appearance of God was in the form of a great fire on the top of the mountain, which gave off thick smoke, for our God is a consuming fire that consumes all the evil in us if we repent, and torments us forever if we refuse it. And the mountain shook like one trembling before the fire, the fog, the thunders and the lightnings.

19.16.0.en: The sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder to declare the presence of God, and in the midst of these manifestations God began to speak with Moses.

19.17.s.en: (5) A warning to the people and the priests

19.17.0.en: God called Moses in the midst of these powerful manifestations to go up to the mountain, and he obeyed and went up.

19.18.0.en: God was concerned for His people, so He stressed to Moses to go down and warn the people for the second time not to approach the mountain and touch it, lest they die.

19.18.1.en: Here God appears with great fear in the Old Testament, while in the New Testament, besides the fear of Him, He has given His people to gather around Him with boldness and love.

19.19.0.en: The sanctification included the priests also, by whom is meant the heads of the clans and families, because the priesthood had not yet been declared by God's choosing Aaron and his sons. What is meant is the care of all the people and their heads to purify themselves, indeed the heads are the more responsible, as an example to the people, to purify themselves.

19.19.1.en: Take care for the purity of your heart, if you are a father or a servant, to be an example for those whom you raise or teach, so that you gain the salvation of your soul and of others.

19.20.0.en: Moses answered God that he had already declared to the people the divine warning not to approach the mountain lest they die, but God in His fatherhood, and because He knows the laxity and weakness of His children, commanded him to go down and warn them for the second time so that none of them should die, and Moses obeyed and went down and warned the people again.

20.0.0.en: After Moses went up and entered the thick fog alone, the Lord spoke with him and gave him the Ten Commandments. The following is noticed in the commandments:

20.0.1.en: 1- Their number is ten, which signifies perfection, that is, the perfection of teaching and guidance, like the ten virgins in the parable of the ten virgins (Mt 25:1-3) and the ten pieces of silver in the parable of the lost piece of silver (Lk 15:8, 9), as God also asks for tithes.

20.0.3.en: a- The first four concern the relation with God, taking the first commandment to be the worship of the one God and the second commandment to be not worshipping images, while the six commandments that follow concern the relation with others.

20.0.4.en: b- There is another division that combines the first and second commandments, so the commandments concerning God are three, and separates the coveting of the neighbor's wife in the tenth commandment from the coveting of his possessions, so the commandments concerning the relation with others become seven.

20.0.5.en: c- The commandments were written on two tablets of stone, so some explain that the first five were written together, and in this way the commandment to honor parents is joined to the relation with God, and this is an exaltation of the fifth commandment.

20.0.6.en: 3- Man's inability: these commandments are negative except the fourth and the fifth, and they reveal man's inability and his sins, but by the grace of the Holy Spirit in the New Testament he is able to carry them out.

20.0.7.en: 4- Christ fulfills the commandments: Christ showed the causes of sin, such as anger, which is the origin of murder, and the look, the origin of adultery; so He confirms the commandments because they are His word, and fulfills them.

20.0.8.en: 5- A summary of the commandments: Christ summed them up in two commandments, which are:

20.0.9.en: a- Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.

20.0.10.en: b- Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself). Lk 10:27)

20.0.11.en: 6- The time of the giving of the commandments: fifty days after the first Passover that was kept in Egypt. After the fourteenth day of the first month to the end of the second month is 45 days, to which is added the day of Moses' going up the mountain and the day of his return to the people, in addition to their sanctification for three days, so the total is fifty days, and this signifies the descent of the Holy Spirit and His sanctification of the Church on the fiftieth day.

20.1.0.en: The first commandment declares the oneness of God and forbids the worship of the gods of the pagan nations surrounding the children of Israel, and these gods appear today in the form of the material things of the world, its positions and all its lusts. The children of Israel fell into the worship of pagan gods and sometimes mixed the worship of God with idols, as when they made the golden calf or the calves that Jeroboam set up, as we mix our spiritual life today with the ideas of the world.

20.2.0.en: The second commandment forbids the making of statues and images of the pagan gods for the purpose of worshipping them, since the making of statues and images of the pagan gods was widespread in the Old Testament. But the use of icons to recall the life of Christ and the saints helps fervent worship. The Orthodox Church prefers the use of icons and not the use of statues like the Catholic Church, because statues give the meaning bodily form and so are more influential, and may draw some to cling to them, such as making statues of the saints, and it is feared that they may distract people from the worship of God, especially if they are statues made with precision and beauty.

20.2.1.en: And God forbids the making of statues and images of the pagan gods because He loves us with the love of a bridegroom for his bride and is jealous over us if we leave Him and are occupied with idols or the material things of the world.

20.2.2.en: God's visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children does not mean that the fathers sin and the innocent children are punished, because in Ezekiel and Jeremiah God utterly rejects this saying when He says, "Ye shall no more use this proverb: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge" (Jer 31:29, 30; Ezek 18:1-25). What is meant is that if the children persist in the errors of their fathers to the third and fourth generation, God punishes them for their clinging to their fathers' errors. It shows God's longsuffering, in that He gives man life to the third and fourth generation that perhaps he may repent, but every person, whether of the fathers or the children, is responsible for his own error and is repaid for it. So He visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, that is, He disciplines them and punishes them in the third and fourth generation because they walked in the sins of their fathers; the fathers are responsible for their sins and for their causing their children to stumble, and the children are responsible for their disobedience to God and their persisting in the sins of their fathers. But if the children obey God and reject the sins of their fathers, they become children blessed by God. At the same time God blesses those who love Him, who hold to His worship and the carrying out of His commandments. It is noticed that the blessing for the obedient is greater than the punishment for those who persist in the evils of their fathers, for He says that the discipline is to the third and fourth generation, while the blessing is to thousands.

20.3.0.en: The third commandment: God wanted to keep His people from uttering the names of the gods of the pagan nations and having recourse to them, so He allowed them to utter His name in all their dealings, but not falsely and in vain or without need, and they are not to utter it with mockery and recklessness or with hypocrisy, because His name is great and holy. In the New Testament we do not swear by it at all in our material dealings, since we have matured spiritually and believe that He is the only God, and we mention it only for sanctification in our prayers (Mt 5:33-37).

20.4.0.en: The fourth commandment: this is the sanctification of the seventh day, because on it God finished the creation of the whole world and rested and was pleased with what He had made; therefore, in glorification of God, He commanded them to sanctify the seventh day, the Sabbath, so that they do no material work on it but devote it to worship, all the people and the slaves also. In the New Testament, God has completed His work in our salvation by the Resurrection, and the glory of Sunday surpassed that of the Sabbath: Christ appeared to His disciples on Sunday, the Holy Spirit descended on Sunday, and since the apostolic age they gathered on Sunday to partake of the Holy Sacraments (Acts 20:7). Therefore the Lord's Day in the New Testament is Sunday, in addition to the continued honoring of the Sabbath also because God completed the creation of the world in it, so there is no fasting without eating on it as on Sunday, except the Saturday of the Light, to remember Christ's being in the tomb.

20.4.1.en: The Jews kept the Sabbath day for the following:

20.4.2.en: 1- Offering greater worship, by doubling the morning and evening burnt offering.

20.4.3.en: 2- Abstaining from material works, including kindling a fire.

20.4.4.en: 3- Permitting a few necessary works such as loosing the animals and watering them and rescuing them if they fell into a pit (Deut 12:11), and moving a limited distance called a Sabbath day's journey, which is about a mile.

20.4.5.en: 4- Being an opportunity for rest for their bodies and their slaves (Deut 5:14, 15).

20.4.6.en: 5- Forbidding going out to gather the manna, because it does not fall on this day.

20.4.7.en: 6- They were allowed to cook food.

20.4.8.en: 7- Besides their worship, they took care to do good.

20.4.9.en: But the elders of the Jews erred through the ages in the sanctification of the Sabbath day: they concerned themselves with not working and set many limits for it, and neglected doing good and worship, as appeared in their opposition to the miracles of Christ on the Sabbath (Jn 5:9). As for the believers in the Church of the New Testament, they honor Sunday by the following:

20.4.10.en: 1- Freeing themselves from material work as far as possible.

20.4.11.en: 2- Attending the Divine Liturgy as much as they can, if their work does not prevent them.

20.4.12.en: 3- Increasing worship, in prayers and readings.

20.4.13.en: 4- Examining the soul, repentance and meditation on God's mercies and love in quiet solitude.

20.4.15.en: 6- Visiting the brethren and those who are far away, to bind them to the Church.

20.4.16.en: 7- Works of goodness such as helping the needy and visiting the sick, the orphans and the weak of every kind.

20.5.0.en: The fifth commandment: because of the parents' toil and their true love, which appears in the raising of their children, God asked the children to honor their parents, not only with kind words and respect but also with obedience, and likewise to provide for their needs when they advance in age and the children become able to help them. This is the only commandment connected with a divine promise, which is length of days upon the earth. What is meant is days filled with peace on earth by God's blessing, and it also signifies the new earth in the Kingdom, where it lasts forever in rest with God. So the meaning of length of days is:

20.5.1.en: 1- Length of the days of life on earth in some cases, for doing good and worship, so that one is a light to others.

20.5.2.en: 2- The abundance of days that a person lives with God, even if his life is short.

20.5.3.en: 3- The extension of the days that a person lives spiritually in the Kingdom of Heaven, that is, the new earth that God grants to whoever obeys His commandments.

20.5.4.en: And in the New Testament God confirms this commandment by Christ's submission to the Virgin and Joseph the carpenter (Lk 3:51) and His obedience to her at the wedding in Cana of Galilee and His working the first miracle in honor of her (Jn 2) and His care for her on the Cross by charging John to take care of her (Jn 19:26, 27). The New Testament also placed one reservation, which is that their obedience be in the Lord, that is, not contrary to His commandments. And Christ was angry with the priests of the Jews who distorted this important commandment by replacing it with offerings on behalf of the parents and neglecting their support by their children (Mt 15:4-6).

20.6.0.en: The sixth commandment: God greatly values the human soul and declares His displeasure at the shedding of blood, as He was displeased with Cain when he killed Abel (Gen 4:8). And if God commanded the killing of the murderer and the adulterer, this was to declare His hatred of sin; but in the New Testament, after spiritual maturity, God hates sin but loves the sinner and is longsuffering toward him that perhaps he may repent.

20.6.1.en: And the sin of murder has many kinds, such as:

20.6.2.en: 1- A man's killing his brother deliberately by any means.

20.6.3.en: 2- A man's killing himself by suicide.

20.6.4.en: 3- Endangering the life of another unintentionally but through negligence, such as housing them in houses about to collapse or not making a parapet for the stairs or the roof (Deut 22:8).

20.6.5.en: 4- Letting loose animals that can kill a person, such as the goring ox (Ex 21:28-32).

20.6.6.en: 5- Putting out poisonous substances without declaring it, so that they kill whoever drinks or eats them without knowing.

20.6.7.en: 6- Drinking wine in large quantities, which can kill a person or hasten his death.

20.6.9.en: 8- Persisting in fornication to the point of severe exhaustion.

20.6.10.en: But killing is permitted in certain cases, which are:

20.6.12.en: 2- Soldiers in war, in obedience to the authorities (Rom 13:4).

20.6.13.en: 3- The authorities' putting to death criminals who harm others.

20.6.14.en: And in the New Testament Christ forbade not only killing but also its first causes, which is anger (Mt 5:21, 22).

20.7.0.en: The seventh commandment: adultery is a great sin in which man sins against God and also against his own body, and it is called uncleanness; by it man defiles himself and the other with whom he committed adultery, and defiles the clothes, the place and the whole land. And in the New Testament Christ warned of the cause of its beginning, which is the evil look, and counted it adultery so that the chaste person might keep away from it (Mt 5:28). Thus Christ rejected every form of adultery such as:

20.7.1.en: 1- Evil sights in the streets and in the media.

20.7.2.en: 2- Women's causing others to stumble by immodest clothing that attracts attention, and by glances and smiles and all means of attracting attention, with the kinds of stumbling fashion.

20.7.7.en: 7- Leniency in joking and the use of the hands.

20.7.8.en: 8- Slipping into the steps of complete adultery.

20.8.0.en: The eighth commandment: theft is a shameful thing that appeared from the beginning of creation, before the giving of the Ten Commandments, when man took what was not his. The first sin was a theft, because it was an eating from the tree from which God had forbidden man to eat, and Laban's accusing Jacob of stealing his idols, and likewise Joseph's accusing his brothers of stealing his cup, was considered a shameful matter deserving the arrest and trial of whoever did it.

20.8.1.en: Theft includes any possessions of another, or even his ideas, and not paying tithes is robbing God. Theft is considered more shameful when it is the plundering of the needy such as the widow and the orphan, or the theft of sacred things. The New Testament called the thief to leave this evil and come out of his selfishness by working to meet his own needs and even to give to the needy (Eph 4:28).

20.9.0.en: The ninth commandment: false witness is lying, and its danger lies in changing the facts, and therefore God hates it, because it acquits the guilty and condemns the innocent and stirs up quarrels among people. It is the work of Satan, who is described as a liar and the father of lies, and therefore the Law provides that testimony be on the mouth of two or three witnesses, to avoid lying as far as possible (Deut 19:15).

20.10.0.en: The tenth commandment: it forbids covetousness and the desiring of what belongs to another, and so it shows the cause of the previous sins, which is the desire of the heart before the deed that the previous commandments forbid. The commandment includes two matters:

20.10.1.en: 1- The neighbor's wife, in which, if a person persists, he falls into adultery.

20.10.2.en: 2- The possessions of another, in which, if a person persists, he falls into theft or murder.

20.10.3.en: And the New Testament has given us the ability to carry out this commandment by the grace of the Holy Spirit.

20.10.4.en: Let God's commandments be before your eyes so that they light your way and keep you from sin; do not be lax and be carried along with the current of the evil world, and if you sin by breaking any commandment, hasten to repentance, and if you find it difficult to carry out in any situation, ask God's help to make it easy for you to carry it out, and so you will receive God's pleasure and blessings and keep your peace.

20.11.0.en: Before the fearful sight of God on the mountain with fire, thunders, lightnings, fog and trumpet, the people were very afraid, so they asked Moses to speak himself with God on the mountain and then come to them in the camp and teach them what God commands.

20.12.0.en: Moses explained to the people the reason for these powerful manifestations that accompanied the appearance of God, which was the testing of the people, that is, fixing the fear of God in their hearts so that they would obey His commandments and not sin against Him by worshipping idols or walking in the evils of the nations.

20.13.0.en: The people stood far from the holy mountain, near their tents, while Moses went up the mountain in the midst of the fog to speak with God.

20.13.1.en: It is good to feel the fear of God so that you reject sin and the semblance of sin, that is, all its causes, even if they seem small, because sin is a defiance of God and a disobedience of His commands and deserves death.

20.14.s.en: (3) Commandments to keep away from the worship of idols

20.14.0.en: God declared to Moses commandments for him to teach to the people, the first of which is that He dwells in heaven, that is, higher than everything they see on earth, and His loftiness above all the pagan gods has appeared in the thunders, lightnings, fire... etc., so that they might worship Him, confident of His power, and reject the idols.

20.15.0.en: He forbade them to make statues, whether of the pagan gods or even for His worship, as they made the golden calf, and not to resemble the nations in making them of silver and gold with their material glitter, because God dwells in heaven and is higher than all material things. It is noticed that they possessed gold and silver from what they had taken from their neighbors in Egypt.

20.16.0.en: "In all places where I record my name": every place in which God declares His glory by speaking with His pious ones or in any heavenly appearances.

20.16.1.en: He commanded the people to offer sacrifices to God on altars made of earth, that is, mud brick, so that their concentration would be on the sacrifice and on pleasing God and not on the form of the altar, and then God blesses them from heaven. These altars suited their wandering in the wilderness or in any other places afterward.

20.17.0.en: Altars may be made of stones, but they are joined to one another with earth and set as they are without carving, so that they do not carve on them shapes like the pagan idols and so turn to the worship of idols through the making of altars.

20.18.0.en: He also commanded them to make the altars directly on the ground and not raised so that they would reach them by steps. The reason is that their nakedness not be uncovered, and what is meant even more than this is their humility, so that the shame of their pride may not be uncovered, and so that they would not resemble the pagans, who built their altars on high places. But afterward they were permitted to make steps, as in Solomon's temple (2 Chr 4:1) and in the days of the prophet Ezekiel (Ezek 43:17).

20.18.1.en: Would that you would be humble when you pray, whether in the church or in the closet, for then your prayer is accepted. And let your concentration be on the sense of God and not on the form of the words or the melodies.

20.18.2.en: The slave, killing and striking in the Law
